cities.legend: The cord-hall stands where the first cord-mothers knotted the names of the Withdrawal, and the Veiled say that whoever cuts a tie in the eldest cord loses his name in every cord in the downs.
cities.economy: Roots and mushrooms of the sour ground, cord-weaving, trade at the downs' edge for iron and salt.

cities.name: Giritren
cities.legend: The oldest stand of red oak bleeds red when it is cut, and the Redbark say it bled for the first time on the day the clans came into the forest, as a welcome or a warning, nobody agrees which.
cities.economy: Hunting, leather dyed with red-oak bark, smuggling on the Organ Coast Road.

figures.name: Harion of Selen
figures.role: First king of the restored crown
figures.biography: A Warden's son of the Weald and of a collateral branch of Aen's line, Harion spent his youth in the War of Unbinding and held the lake port beneath the Parim bluff for Selen's companies. Crowned at Parim in 4A 1, he rebuilt the roads and granaries, gave the dominions the Charters of Parim and chartered the Houses of the First Light because they had kept the Vale fed; he is called the Restorer in every chronicle.

figures.name: Hezar of Hugomon
figures.biography: A lake-house captain who brought his company home alive from the Ember Lands campaign, Hezar was given the new march across the Grey Hills by Edran in 2A 12 and built its first towers facing south. The march-folk remember him as the only man in the Alliance who expected the war to come back.

figures.name: Ostvar of Deoreh
figures.role: Founder of the toll-lordship of Fotan
figures.biography: A Leren sea-captain who married into the Aenoran ferry-house at the strait's narrowest crossing, Ostvar stretched the first toll-chain across the landing at Deoreh and made the Order's tribute ships pay to pass. The Order burned his tower twice; he rebuilt it twice, and his house has held the strait ever since.

figures.name: Deolof
figures.biography: A head of the watch-families who opened the gorge forts to the Unbinding's companies in 3A 1244, Deolof became the first Pass-Lord under the Pass Charter of 4A 3 and had the forts' names read at the gorge every year. His son's night alone in the gorge gave the vale's town its name.

figures.name: Klungor
figures.role: First Captain of the Klungori Guard
figures.biography: Grandson of a captain of the Unbinding's last company, Klungor took the western foot of the South Pass for land instead of pay with two hundred sworn men and founded the company that still bears his name; he swore the Lamp Truce for it in 4A 96.

figures.name: Saelor of Dalvis
figures.role: First Chief Speaker of the Eight Towns
figures.biography: A toll-master of Dalvis who ended the two-summer toll war of the south-eastern roads by persuading the eight towns to swear one confederacy at Saelori in 4A 774, Saelor laid down the rule that no family holds the Chief Speaker's office twice running.

figures.name: Tamric Bellaren
figures.role: Master of the bell-founders in the Bell Riot
figures.biography: Master of Horlomon's bell-founders when the crown doubled the tax on bells, Tamric rang every bell in the guild-city for three days and nights in 4A 1610 until the Royal Council rescinded it; the guild-hall bell still rings his name on the riot's anniversary.

figures.name: Hallec of the Gate
figures.role: Pass-Lord of Kingson in the Toll of Silver
figures.biography: The Pass-Lord who doubled the toll on elven silver in 4A 1689 and so earned the vale a winter of elven silence, Hallec signed the Kingson Reckoning in 4A 1690 that halved it again; the vale remembers him as clever, the elves as greedy.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Peace of the One Crown
lawsAndCustoms.summary: No lord of Aenor may make war on another without the crown's judgement; breaking the Peace is the first meaning of rebellion in Aenoran law, and the Concord courts still cite it in every border quarrel.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The twenty-six charter-seats
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The Charters of Parim gave each dominion seats in the Concord Council in proportion to the levies it owed the common defence, twenty-six in all, and a dominion that joins a neighbour keeps the neighbour's seat. In 4A 1748 Selen and Noleksun hold three each; Konori, Hunhun, Kingson, Herez, Kilinti, Safeton, Freshon, Pazoma and Orohaf two each; the Klungori Guard and Kunhrim one each.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Quiet Law
lawsAndCustoms.summary: No ranger draws a bow on another ranger, no standing tree is felled without the moot's leave, and every stranger is given one night's shelter before he is asked his business.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Reading of Names
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Every year at the pass forts the names of those who held the passes against the Order are read aloud, and every watch-family's child is presented at the reading in the year it is born.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Old Promise and the harvest-share
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The small folk carry a share of every harvest up to the giants' halls, and no stranger enters the Hilorn valleys without a giant's leave; the giants say the promise is theirs to keep and not a god's.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The cairn count
lawsAndCustoms.summary: A giant leaves one stone on a cairn for each winter of life, and a dispute between clans is judged by which party can name the older cairn; no giant is ever asked how many stones are in his own.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Iron Charter
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The hold sells iron to the crown and keeps every elf off its roads, and since 4A 1612 its black powder, made by an art learned from the western hold of Hrennost, goes to the crown and to nobody else.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Lamp Truce
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Sworn over a lit lamp in 4A 96: the goblins keep the caves, the dwarves the galleries, and nobody crosses into the other's dark; the lamp is relit at the Hungohon tower whenever the truce is renewed.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Tide-Oath
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The queen is chosen from the daughters of the five Isle Houses by their eldest women, inheritance runs through daughters, and every house gives its dead to the tide by the same rite.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The raising on the felt
lawsAndCustoms.summary: A King of Konori is lifted on a white felt by the heads of the Hundreds at the ford of Arrovez, and a king who loses their trust is set down on it.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The cords of the mothers
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Among the Veiled and the Redbark descent runs through mothers, names are knotted on the mother's cord at birth, and a stolen name is a cut tie; the years are counted by the ties of the eldest cord.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Golden Charters
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Privileges sold by the Golden King: freedom from royal tolls and a town court of its own, bought by Freshon in 4A 1731 and Pazoma in 4A 1734 at prices that left both in the Golden Court's debt.
